title: ACCOUNTING SPECIALIST
ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounting Specialist is responsible for balancing and submitting remits, posting refunds, and managing commission and cost reimbursements. They also handle payment allocations and issue refunds to consumers within the firm's system of record.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a High School Diploma or GED and at least 2 years of accounting experience. Proficiency in Excel, including Pivot Tables and VLOOKUP, is required along with strong problem-solving and communication skills.
description_text:
Description
***$1,000 Sign-on Bonus After Successfully Completing 90 Days***
Summary:
Messerli Kramer, a trusted Twin Cities law firm since 1965, is looking for a full-time Accounting Specialist to join our team in Plymouth, MN. Under general supervision and following established procedures, the Accounting Specialist is responsible for a variety of accounting duties and tasks.

Essential Functions and Duties:
Balancing and submitting remits
Posting refunds using our system
Posting commission and cost reimbursement from our clients into our system
Sending Firm Fee funds downtown
Issuing refunds to our consumers
Correcting payment allocations in our system of record
Additional Responsibilities assigned by management
Benefits & Perks Include:
Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance
HSA & FSA Accounts
401K, with 4% company contribution (after 1 year of service)
Paid time off (17 days per year)
Paid holidays off (7 days per year + a floating holiday)
Company Paid Life Insurance
Employee Assistance Program
Building amenities include: Free parking, onsite restaurant, & onsite free gym
Requirements
Required Education & Experience:
High School Diploma/GED
Degree in Accounting preferred, but not required
2+ years working accounting experience
Experience with Excel (Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP)
Competencies:
Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
Extreme attention to detail
Clear written and verbal communication skills
An ability to multi-task and work in a fast-paced environment
Self-motivation
Work Environment and Physical Demands:
This role operates in a professional office setting, routinely working with standard office equipment. Generally, due to the nature of this office position, the person in this role would be required to talk and hear, sit or stand for long period of time, and use their hands and fingers, to handle and feel. Occasionally required to walk, reach with arms and hand, climb or balance, and to stoop, kneel, or crouch. Regularly required to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Vision abilities required by the job include close vision.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions and to meet job requirements.

All applicants must pass a criminal background check, drug screening, and credit check, before commencing employment with Messerli & Kramer, P.A.

Wage Disclaimer: The starting wage for this position is $19.00-$25.00/hour.

About Us:
Messerli Kramer is a leading law firm in the Twin Cities founded in 1965 with locations in Minneapolis, St. Paul and Plymouth, Minnesota. We have a well-earned reputation within the business community of providing sound, reasoned and comprehensive legal advice. Our professionals take the time to listen and understand their legal issues within the larger framework of their business as a whole. Known for our dedication and responsiveness, our attorneys and staff are focused on finding pragmatic solutions and producing remarkable results for our clients.

Messerli Kramer serves individuals and businesses through three unique, yet complementary, divisions. We represent a variety of clients—from large corporations, banks and closely-held businesses—to individuals seeking divorce and family law or estate planning services. Our clients trust us to help them navigate the myriad of legal issues that confront them in their business and personal lives.

org_linkedin_description:
WHO WE ARE

At Messerli Kramer, we’ve spent 60 years building a reputation as a firm of “attorneys and advisors” – or, as we like to say, a place where the law isn’t always the best answer. Our attorneys come from an array of backgrounds, and in everything we do, we put people first – not just with our clients, but also with our employees. That means making the right decision at every turn, even if it doesn’t always benefit our bottom line. That’s what makes a healthy work culture. That’s what makes us Messerli Kramer. 

WHAT WE DO
 
Since 1965 we’ve fostered a collaborative environment, one in which the breadth and depth of services available to our clients isn’t limited by ability. That’s why we maintain three offices, each of which focuses on a different aspect of corporate and individual needs – from consumer collections and creditor remedies in Plymouth, to full-service corporate and litigation needs in Minneapolis, to high-powered governmental lobbying in St. Paul. We believe that encouragement, support and respect for one another is what fosters an enviable environment, and that all starts with investing in the right people – with investing in attorneys and advisors.

WHY WE’RE DIFFERENT
 
Our focus of providing sound advice for all clients, regardless of the impact on our bottom line, comes from our ability to operate as boldly independent. With Minnesota-based ownership and a diversified practice distribution designed to withstand economic swings, we are able to nimbly navigate client needs and provide top-notch service at every stage of an interaction.

title: Senior Accountant
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Accountant is responsible for key accounting functions including reconciliations, journal entries, payroll, and fixed asset management. They will also lead month-end and year-end close processes while supporting financial reporting and audit preparation.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree in accounting or finance and possess relevant professional experience in general ledger accounting. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and accounting software, along with excellent analytical and communication skills, is required.
description_text:
Description
Position Summary
We are seeking an experienced and highly organized Senior Accountant to join the Business Office at Southwest Christian School. This position is responsible for key accounting functions including account reconciliations, journal entries, payment-service activity, fixed assets, tax and audit preparation, payroll accounting, and financial recordkeeping associated with various departments. The Senior Accountant will work closely with Business Office leadership and departments throughout the school to maintain accurate financial records, strengthen accounting processes, and support timely financial reporting.

The successful candidate will combine strong technical accounting skills with a collaborative and service-oriented approach. This person will take ownership of assigned accounting areas, identify discrepancies before they become problems, maintain well-organized documentation, and build productive relationships with colleagues across the school. Just as importantly, the Senior Accountant will recognize that accurate financial stewardship is an important part of supporting the school's Christian mission and the students, families, faculty, and staff it serves.


Essential Responsibilities
Prepare monthly bank reconciliations and investigate and resolve reconciling items
Record and reconcile activity from payment platforms and services, including Stripe, Square, Jumbula, Hudl, and similar systems
Record and reconcile transactions related to donations, banking activity, and investments
Prepare advanced recurring and other journal entries
Prepare and file applicable sales tax returns
Maintain fixed asset records, including additions, disposals, and related accounting activity
Prepare schedules, reconciliations, supporting documentation, and other PBC ("prepared by client") materials for annual tax return preparation
Coordinate and prepare PBC schedules and documentation for the annual financial statement audit.
Maintain and reconcile accounting records related to various school departments and programs including but not limited to Advancement, Athletics, Booster Club, PTO
Lead month-end and year-end close processes
Research accounting discrepancies and recommend corrections or process improvements
Support Business Office leadership with financial reporting, analysis, and other accounting projects as needed
Requirements
Education & Experience
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or a closely related field
Relevant professional accounting experience with demonstrated responsibility for general ledger accounting, reconciliations, and journal entries
Strong understanding of generally accepted accounting principles and accounting controls
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and accounting systems
Ability to independently prioritize responsibilities and meet monthly, annual, audit, and tax deadlines
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality regarding financial, employee, donor, and family information

Preferred Qualifications
Experience with QuickBooks; experience with a system implementation from QuickBooks to NetSuite, Intacct, or similar software highly preferred
Accounting experience within a nonprofit organization; experience in a private or independent school is highly preferred
Experience preparing supporting schedules and documentation for external audits and tax filings
Familiarity with contribution/donation accounting and reconciling records with various school programs
CPA or progress toward CPA certification is a plus

Personal & Spiritual Characteristics
Is deeply committed to a consistent daily walk with our Savior, Jesus Christ, through prayer, devotional study, and church membership
Demonstrates the spiritual maturity, academic ability, and personal leadership qualities to “train up a child in the way he should go” (Proverbs 22:6)
Possesses the ability to work gracefully with faculty and school staff in a supporting role to encourage a unified and successful educational program
Cooperates with administrators, department chairpersons, and other school leadership to implement policies and procedures as they pertain to the daily operation of the School
Follow Matthew 18 principle in dealing with conflict with faculty and staff
Demonstrates the ability to accept and carry out responsibilities and make competent, professional decisions
Eagerly participates in professional development activities and the evaluation process with a desire to grow professionally, spiritually, and personally throughout the career in education
Maintains a professional personal appearance that is a Christian role model of cleanliness, modesty, good taste, and is in accordance with school policy


Work Environment
The work environment at Southwest Christian School is consistent with a typical school setting. The employee normally works indoors but may be required to be outdoors in unpredictable temperatures to occasionally monitor outdoor activities, attend programs, or move between buildings. The noise level in the environment is usually low to moderate but may become loud occasionally. The employee is required to interact with others within the school community, including parents and other caregivers. Reasonable accommodations can be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.


Additional Duties / Responsibilities
This job description is not intended to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required as an active participant in the mission of Southwest Christian School. Additional duties are regularly performed by the individuals currently holding this position and additional duties may be assigned.

title: Deposit Compliance Specialist
ai_core_responsibilities: The Deposit Compliance Specialist performs specialized functions related to BSA, AML, CFT, and OFAC policies to ensure regulatory compliance across bank operations. Responsibilities include conducting compliance testing, monitoring customer transactions, managing vendor risk assessments, and performing audits.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a high school diploma or GED and a minimum of two years of banking experience. Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills are required, along with knowledge of federal and state banking regulations.
description_text:
Description
Summary Under the general supervision of the BSA/Deposit Compliance Officer, this position independently performs a wide variety of general or specialized functions in regard to Deposit Compliance, Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) and Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Policy and Procedures. Conducts compliance testing and monitoring of policy, procedures, and customer transactions against all applicable laws and regulations throughout the company. Assists Chief Risk Officer in testing and monitoring with compliance and risk reviews, as needed.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned. 

Bank Secrecy Act
· Assist the bank’s BSA Officer to ensure compliance with BSA and FinCEN requirements.
· Provides assistance with Bank Secrecy Act Administration ensuring regulatory deadlines are met.
o Overall review of customer transactions/monitoring
o Currency Transaction Report (CTR) filings
o Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) write-ups & monitoring
o Subpoena and summons requests
o Reviews alerts generated from the BSA software
· Review Currency & Large Dollar reports.
· Conduct Customer Due Diligence & Enhanced Due Diligence reviews.
· Perform the FinCEN 314(a) reviews every two weeks.
· Assist with reviews of new Customer Information Files (CIF) records for compliance with Customer Information Program (CIP).
· Monitor year-end reporting on all non-resident aliens.
· Monitor potential OFAC matches and takes appropriate action to escalate when necessary.
· Review monetary instrument logs for anomalous activity.
· Assist with annual reviews of customer exceptions from currency transaction reporting.

Deceased Customers
· Completes Estate inventories. This may include working with the estate attorney.
· Review required documentation for deceased customers.
· Work with bank staff in obtaining appropriate documentation on deceased customers.
· Process interest adjustments for deceased customers and beneficiaries for year-end reporting.

Garnishments
· Processes and tracks all garnishment/levy requests.

Third-Party Vendor Management
· Assists Chief Risk Officer with annual vendor risk assessments and periodic monitoring.

Checkback
· Performs checkback on all new CIF records and maintenance.
· Performs checkback on all new DDA, CDA and SDB and maintenance.
· Performs checkback on IRA’s
· Performs checkback on Reg CC Holds.
· Performs checkback on beneficial ownership documentation.
· Indexes all “scanned” documents in Director Software.

Compliance
· Assist with conducting compliance training for the bank’s board of directors and bank staff.
· Conduct compliance reviews for each area of the Bank’s operations.
· Perform surprise cash drawer audits at all VisionBank locations. Provide compliance support to VisionBank staff.
· Assist with year-end system reviews, including IRAs, 1099 form reviews, CIF records, etc.
· Performs year-end processing and reviews for IRAs, including excess contributions, and ensuring required minimum distributions (RMD) have been satisfied.
· Processes required reporting on deceased IRA customers and beneficiary payouts.

IRAs (provides back up support)
· Reviews new IRA files and all IRA transactions for accuracy.
· Prepares and processes all required IRA documentation to customers, including annual documentation.
· Performs year-end processing and reviews for IRAs including excess contributions and ensuring Required Minimum Distributions (RMD) have been satisfied.
· Oversees and administers all RMDs.
· Processes required reporting on deceased IRA customers and beneficiary payouts.

Additional Responsibilities
· Monitor overdrawn account activity.
· Assist with Return Mail.
· Prepare management reports as needed.
· Performs special projects as assigned.
· Demonstrate compliance with all bank regulations and keeps up to date on regulation changes.
· Adheres to all State and Federal Banking regulations.
· Participates in civic activities to promote growth and development of the community and a positive image of the bank.

Requirements
Supervisory Responsibilities
This job has no supervisory responsibilities.

Core Competencies
To be successful in this role, the employee must demonstrate sound judgment, professionalism, integrity, and a commitment to the organization's mission, values, and policies. The position requires strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and project management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and consistently deliver high-quality, accurate, and timely results.

The employee who is successful in this role, communicates effectively, both verbally and in writing, builds collaborative relationships, provides exceptional customer service, and works productively with diverse teams. This role requires initiative, accountability, continuous learning, and the ability to make informed decisions while maintaining confidentiality and exercising good judgment.

Employees are expected to contribute to a positive and inclusive work environment, demonstrate leadership appropriate to their role, embrace innovation and continuous improvement, use organizational resources responsibly, and maintain a strong commitment to safety, quality, dependability, and ethical conduct.
Supervisory positions are additionally expected to effectively lead, develop, and support employees through coaching, delegation, performance management, and change leadership.
Qualifications 
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience
High school diploma or general education degree (GED). A minimum of two years of banking experience is required. Preferred experience in compliance.

Language Skills
Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to write simple correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees of the organization.

Mathematical Skills
Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide.

Reasoning Ability
Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out detailed but uninvolved written or oral instructions. Ability to deal with problems involving a few concrete variables in standardized situations.

Computer Skills
To perform this job successfully, an individual should have knowledge of Microsoft Suite software.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations Other Skills and Abilities

Other Qualifications
· Knowledge of compliance laws and regulations including federal and state banking regulations.
· Must be able to travel to all bank locations.

Physical Demands 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 20 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and color vision.

Work Environment 
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
VisionBank is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, pregnancy status, sex, age, marital status, medical conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran and/or disability status.

title: Accounting Associate
ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounting Associate manages day-to-day financial operations including accounts payable, general ledger reconciliations, and expense reporting. They also provide administrative support to school departments and customer service to families regarding tuition and financial aid.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must hold an associate or bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or a related field, or possess equivalent relevant experience. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong organizational and communication skills are required for this role.
description_text:
Description
Position Summary
We are seeking a detail-oriented, service-minded Accounting Associate to join the Business Office at Southwest Christian School. This position plays an important role in the day-to-day accounting operations of the school, including accounts payable, general ledger reconciliations, deposits, expense reporting, and support for families, vendors, and school departments.

The ideal candidate is organized, dependable, comfortable working with accounting systems and detailed financial information, and committed to providing excellent service. The Accounting Associate should approach their work with integrity, discretion, collaboration, and a desire to support the mission of Southwest Christian School.

A successful Accounting Associate will be someone others can rely on for accurate work, timely follow-through, and helpful service. This person will understand that strong financial administration supports every part of the school's mission, from serving families to equipping faculty and staff with the resources they need.


Essential Responsibilities
Enter and process accounts payable transactions and maintain accurate supporting documentation
Prepare and set up accounts payable payment runs
Perform general ledger reconciliations and research discrepancies
Prepare basic recurring journal entries
Distribute accounting and financial reports to department managers
Communicate with vendors and assist with vendor setup, account questions, documentation, and issue resolution
Prepare and distribute invoices related to facility rentals
Post deposits and scan and maintain appropriate backup documentation
Provide basic customer service assistance to families regarding tuition and financial aid account questions
Review Ramp expense reports for compliance with school policies, appropriate receipts, and accurate general ledger coding
Maintain organized and accurate accounting records in accordance with school policies and procedures
Assist members of the Business Office with other accounting and administrative responsibilities as needed

Requirements
Education & Experience
Required Qualifications
Associate or bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant accounting experience
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy
Ability to manage multiple responsibilities, meet deadlines, and follow established financial procedures
Strong organizational, communication, and customer service skills
Ability to handle financial and personal information with discretion and confidentiality
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and the ability to learn accounting and financial software
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with QuickBooks or similar accounting software
Experience with Ramp or another expense and corporate card management platform
Previous accounting or bookkeeping experience in a nonprofit organization, private school, church, or similar mission-driven environment
Experience with accounts payable, general ledger reconciliations, and expense reporting

Personal & Spiritual Characteristics
Is deeply committed to a consistent daily walk with our Savior, Jesus Christ, through prayer, devotional study, and church membership
Demonstrates the spiritual maturity, academic ability, and personal leadership qualities to “train up a child in the way he should go” (Proverbs 22:6)
Possesses the ability to work gracefully with faculty and school staff in a supporting role to encourage a unified and successful educational program
Cooperates with administrators, department chairpersons, and other school leadership to implement policies and procedures as they pertain to the daily operation of the School
Follow Matthew 18 principle in dealing with conflict with faculty and staff
Demonstrates the ability to accept and carry out responsibilities and make competent, professional decisions
Eagerly participates in professional development activities and the evaluation process with a desire to grow professionally, spiritually, and personally throughout the career in education
Maintains a professional personal appearance that is a Christian role model of cleanliness, modesty, good taste, and is in accordance with school policy


Work Environment
The work environment at Southwest Christian School is consistent with a typical school setting. The employee normally works indoors but may be required to be outdoors in unpredictable temperatures to occasionally monitor outdoor activities, attend programs, or move between buildings. The noise level in the environment is usually low to moderate but may become loud occasionally. The employee is required to interact with others within the school community, including parents and other caregivers. Reasonable accommodations can be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

title: Accounting Staff Generalist - Hotels, Development and Real Estate
ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounting Staff Generalist is responsible for managing accounts payable and receivable, including processing invoices, collections, and vendor communications. They will also assist with month-end closing activities and contribute to process improvement initiatives.
ai_requirements_summary: The ideal candidate should have a passion for accounting and experience in maintaining accurate financial records. Proficiency in managing customer payments, billing discrepancies, and ledger reconciliation is required for this role.
description_text:
Description
Noble House Hotels and Resorts owns, manages, or operates a portfolio of 20+ luxury, independent hotels and resorts around the country and Mexico. We are seeking an Accounting Staff Generalist for our corporate office located in Kirkland, WA.

If you have a passion for numbers, accounting and travel, this is the perfect combination!

Requirements
What You Do:
Accounting Staff Generalist will play a crucial role in maintaining accounts payable, entering invoices, reviewing statements, contacting vendors, issuing 1099s for multiple properties within our company.
To be successful as the Accounting Staff Generalist position, you:
Process customer invoices accurately and efficiently 
Generate and send invoices to customers in a timely manner.
Review and verify invoices for completeness, accuracy, and proper authorization.
Manage customer payments and collections 
Record and apply customer payments, including checks, electronic funds transfers, and credit card transactions.
Monitor accounts receivable aging reports and follow up on overdue accounts.
Communicate with customers to resolve billing discrepancies and payment issues.
Maintain accurate records of all accounts receivable transactions 
Reconcile accounts receivable ledger to ensure all payments are accounted for and properly posted.
Prepare and process adjustments, credits, and refunds as needed.
Assist in month-end closing activities related to accounts receivable, including accruals and reporting.
Contribute to process improvement initiatives 
Identify opportunities to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of the accounts receivable process.
Collaborate with other departments to streamline billing and collection procedures.
Participate in special projects and initiatives as assigned.

The OFFER:
In return, you are rewarded with a competitive compensation package including competitive pay, On-Demand Pay – Your Pay before Payday, health insurance (medical, dental, vision), 401k plan with employer matching, Paid Time Off, holidays, and Discounted Food & Hotel Discounts at Noble House Hotels & Resorts nationwide.

OUR CULTURE | Individual Distinction, Collective Soul
The Noble House Hotels & Resorts philosophy emphasizes "location, distinction, and soul." Our properties are not a "one-size-fits-all." And neither are our team members. What makes us at Noble House Hotels & Resorts lies within our team. We are a group of individuals that share a passion for hospitality. We let our personalities shine, and we like to have fun.

Become a part of our Noble CommUNITY- We take pride in providing initiatives through our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Accessibility (DEIA), Green and Wellness committees. Join us in sharing your thoughts, perspectives, and enthusiasm!

Noble House Hotels & Resorts are proud to encourage and support an environment where everyone can be a successful team member (come as they are) as their true authentic self. We are an equal opportunity workplace and employer that does not discriminate based on race, color, disability, gender/sex, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, veteran status, or any other protected status. We are committed to building a team (rooted in family) and a workplace where we are all able to be successful based solely on our individual qualifications, experience, abilities and job performance.
